### CNN values your feedback

# Power outages, fuel bans and no summer camps: Ukraine steps up pressure on Russia by targeting Crimea

![Zahra Ullah](https://media.cnn.com/api/v1/images/stellar/prod/230328102842-zahra-ullah-byline.jpg?c=16x9&q=h_270,w_480,c_fill/c_thumb,g_face,w_50,h_50)
![Cars queue for fuel at a gas station after the authorities restricted fuel sales amid a supply shortage following Ukrainian attacks on logistics routes in Sevastopol, Crimea, on June 1.](https://media.cnn.com/api/v1/images/stellar/prod/2026-06-24t033905z-736110689-rc2zklatl3sd-rtrmadp-3-ukraine-crisis-attack-crimea.JPG?c=original&q=w_1041,c_fill)

Power outages have continued to plague Sevastopol, the largest city in Russian-controlled Crimea, following repeated, intensified Ukrainian strikes on the peninsula.

The Kremlin-installed governor of the city, Mikhail Razvozhayev, said Thursday that restrictions had been introduced across the city and urged residents to reduce the load on the power grid. Ukraine’s drone forces commander [Robert Brovdi](https://t.me/robert_magyar/2518) said Kyiv had attacked Sevastopol’s main power substation seven times in the early hours of Wednesday.

Russia annexed Crimea in 2014, a move widely condemned by the international community, after the Maidan protests ousted Ukraine’s then pro-Kremlin president, Viktor Yanukovych. The port city of Sevastopol was historically home to the headquarters for Russia’s Black Sea Fleet.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensk

Kremlin-backed authorities in annexed Crimea declared a state of emergency on Friday afternoon following days of intense Ukrainian attacks that have knocked out power in parts of the peninsula and compounded ongoing challenges for residents, including fuel shortages and restrictions on public transit.

“This state of emergency will remain in effect until the situation improves,” Sevastopol Governor Mikhail Razvozhayev [said](https://t.me/razvozhaev/21764 "said") in a Telegram video address announcing a citywide state of emergency.

# Russian-Occupied Crimea Declares State of Emergency as Ukraine Ups Strikes

Published

Jun 26, 2026 at 10:14 AM EDT

![Brendan Cole](/default-avatar.svg)

Senior Reporter

A state of emergency has been announced in Russian-occupied Crimea following a spike in Ukrainian drone attacks that have caused fuel shortages and power outages.

Sergei Aksyonov, the Moscow-appointed head of Crimea, announced the measures in a post on social media, which comes as Ukraine continues its bombardment of ⁠energy sites and other targets in Russia, as well as in the peninsula annexed in 2014.

The return of Crimea is one of Kyiv’s stated war aims following Moscow’s full-scale invasion in 2022, and the peninsula has been hit hard by drone attacks and long queues at ⁠gas stations in recent months.

#### Read More on World

Aksyonov said that the energy supply in Crimea “remains difficult” and that he hoped that the energy supply in the city of Sevastopol would be fully restored.

The emergency declaration would remain in place until the situation improved, he added, without specifying further.

![Black smoke rising from the Russian oil producer Gazprom Neft's Moscow oil refinery on June 18, 2026.](https://assets.newsweek.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/GettyImages-2281563924-6a4c22.jpg?w=1600&quality=80&webp=1)

*This is a developing story and will be updated when more information is available.*

Official sources from both Russia and Ukraine have confirmed a prisoner exchange that took place on Friday, involving 160 prisoners of war from each side.

Russian state news agencies reported the exchange, citing the Russian Ministry of Defense.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky also confirmed the prison swap.
